context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: The evidence is only a redacted fragment (`const «SECRET»)`), so the exact variable and route can't be identified. Treat it as a response that serialises a whole record and change it like this: (1) Don't pass the full model, nested record or secret value to `res.json`/`res.send` or into a response object. Build an explicit response shape with an allow-list instead, for example `const dto = { id: user.id, displayName: user.displayName };`, and return only `dto`. (2) Leave out secrets, tokens, password hashes, API keys and internal IDs, along with any Personal Data Elements (such as email, phone, address or government IDs) the requester isn't entitled to see for the Purpose the data was collected for under §6(1). (3) Put the allow-list in one shared serializer or DTO function, such as `toPublicUser(record)`, and use it on every route that returns this record, so field limits match across routes as Rule 6(1)(b) requires. If the requester's role allows extra fields, add them through separate role-specific serializers. (4) For nested or related records, use explicit `select`/projection in the query, such as Prisma `select` or Mongoose `.select()`, rather than loading everything and stripping fields afterwards. (5) Add a test for each route that checks the response contains exactly the allowed keys and no secret or out-of-purpose fields.
